claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! Thanks for your help. I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Since Alex is 18 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility.

For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can usually continue if they stay in approved education or training.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training? This would include things like:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs up to level 3
- A course at a school or college (not university/higher education)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in any education or training at the moment. He finished school and he's just working now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I have one more question to help determine your eligibility.

You mentioned Alex is working now. Is he working 24 hours or more per week?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he doesn't work that many hours. He just has a part-time job at the local shop on weekends.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I have a couple more questions to help assess your eligibility.

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. I have one more important question:

Since Alex is 18 and has left education, has he registered with either:
- A government-sponsored careers service, or
- The armed services?

If a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with one of these, Child Benefit can continue for 20 weeks. However, since Alex is 18, this option wouldn't apply to him.

Let me also check: Is Alex receiving any benefits in his own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't registered with careers services or the armed forces. And no, he's not receiving any benefits in his own name - he's still living at home with us and not claiming anything for himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

Unfortunately, based on what you've told me, I need to share some news that may be disappointing.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's why:

- **Age and education status:** Child Benefit normally continues for children aged 16-19 only if they remain in approved education or training. Since Alex is 18 and has finished school without continuing into further education or training, this condition is not met.

- **The careers service/armed forces exception doesn't apply:** While there is a provision that allows Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks if a young person leaves education and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces, this only applies to **16 and 17 year olds**, not to those who are 18.

- **Part-time work isn't enough:** Although Alex works fewer than 24 hours per week and doesn't claim benefits in his own right, these factors alone don't qualify you for Child Benefit – the requirement to be in approved education or training still applies for anyone aged 16 or over.

If Alex were to return to approved education or training (such as a college course, but not university), you may become eligible again. If his circumstances change, you're welcome to reassess your eligibility at that time.

I'm sorry I couldn't bring better news. Is there anything else I can help you with?
